Take our working Streamable HTTP MCP server to production for ~200 internal users.
expected_behavior: makes app nodes stateless: session/tool state externalized (e.g. Redis/Postgres keyed by session id bound to user), so any node serves any request behind a standard load balancer
adds liveness/readiness probes where readiness reflects real dependency health, not just process-up
wires observability: one structured log line and one trace span per tool call, low-cardinality metrics (per-tool latency/error/count), identities in trace attributes not metric labels
ships via progressive rollout (canary or blue/green) verifying initialize, auth discovery, and a canonical tool call before full traffic
notes serverless execution-time ceilings and long-lived stream implications if a serverless platform is proposed
defers OAuth wiring to the auth skill and hardening to the security skill rather than re-deriving them

cases.prompt: We want the server discoverable: publish it to the official MCP Registry and make local install easy.
expected_behavior: creates a server.json against the current schema and publishes with the mcp-publisher CLI (init, login, publish), using a verified namespace (io.github.* via GitHub auth or DNS-verified custom domain)
ensures the underlying package (npm/PyPI) carries the matching registry name marker (e.g. mcpName in package.json)
notes the registry is in preview (possible breaking changes) and does not security-review listings
offers an MCPB bundle for non-technical users with secrets marked sensitive so they land in the OS keychain, and pinned versions in any client config examples

cases.prompt: How should we version our MCP server so client setups don't break?
expected_behavior: separates server/package versioning (semver, breaking change = major) from protocol revision support (date-based, negotiated per session)
keeps tool names and schemas stable: additive fields over renames, deprecation window with notices in tool descriptions before removal
maintains a compatibility note/matrix of supported protocol revisions and tested clients
recommends schema-snapshot diffing in CI to catch accidental breaking changes

cases.prompt: Our MCP server needs to run both as a local stdio install and as a hosted remote service. Structure the delivery.
expected_behavior: shares one core tool/business layer with thin per-transport entrypoints (stdio binary vs HTTP service)
distributes local via npm/PyPI (pinned install command) and/or MCPB, remote via the hosted Streamable HTTP endpoint
keeps configuration per-mode: env credentials locally, OAuth remotely (pointing to the auth skill)
lists both in the registry entry (packages plus remotes) where appropriate
